prep.gitTest: Last week we began to work with the gaming engine unity. As we got more familiar with the engine we started to move 3d objects around our little "game" by implementing code with Microsoft Visual Studios.
prep.access: My Git seems to be accessible and ready.
prep.video1: After watching this first video I understand that we are now trying to see how a game is made in the simplest pipeline we can possibly use.
prep.video2: I understand that mindset is a very important factor when it comes to game development and is crucial to success. This video goes in depth on how a positive mindset can help foster the qualities and encouragement that developers use to think both inside and outside of the box.
prep.video3: This third video goes over building a solid folder structure and why its so important. A simple answer to why its important is to have an easier time managing your project and also looks more inviting to people who see your projects folders wanting to learn more about your game and what you used to make it. When having a more organized set of folders it serves as a navigating system for whoever opens it such as a group member, classmate, or even AI.
prep.video4: As this video goes over Documentation, which is pretty much rough understanding of your game meaning a brief summary including title of the game and its design as well as a game overview just explaining the gameplay, functions, and its targeted audience. This is said to be important because its like reading what you are about to get into. Many major games have used documentations and added them to their page. An example would be GTA V with their page having a trailer and a brief summary of what awaits you in the city of Los Santos.
prep.video5: In video #5 "IntroToUnity" professor goes over how we can skip starting from scratch and use templates because depending on what you want your game to look like it can save you almost hours of work. He also shows how to fix common problems such as  decompression issues when downloading templates. Then goes over how to navigate and make changes to your game with it either being adding a new camera perspective or even in games structural changes.
prep.video6: In video #6 "import custom player" professor goes over how we can change our character to our liking. There are plenty of different downloadable characters under the site mixamo with it just being as easy of just dragging the downloaded file into unity.
prep.opinion: This pipeline can definitely play a huge part in either an already existing or new story because using documentation our game overview is just our entire story summarized and giving a brief idea on what to expect. Also the introduction to character changes is huge because our character or main protagonist can now have distinct physical features that can be recognized throughout the community such as mega mans arm cannon.
prep.questions: How to change the hitboxes of certain characters?

huddle.mission:
A 2-D wave-based game with escalating difficulty as the rounds progress. Online/offline, up to 4 players total.
The main goal is to see how far you can get until the enemies overwhelm you and defeat you.
huddle.framework: P2P can be advantageous in the development by guiding us to the end point of where our team wants the game to stand. There is not much of a story to derive from this type of game, as opposed to other single-player, story mode games, but an underlying story to the characters can help immersify the fans.
